name: Molasses Cake With Salty-Sweet Whipped Butter

cookwares.name: 9- by 5-inch loaf pan (preferably a straight-sided pan aka a Pullman loaf pan)

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, room temperature and cubed
light syrup, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: For the Cake: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 325°F. Grease a 9- by 5-inch (preferably straight-sided) loaf pan with nonstick spray (see notes.) Line pan with a 5-by-18-inch piece of parchment so the length of the pan is covered by a 1-inch overhang. (This creates a sling that can be used to remove the cake from the pan later.)
In a medium bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rye flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and black pepper. Set aside.

In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat molasses, butter, and 100 g (1/2 cup) sugar on medium-high speed until light and fluffy, pausing every so often to scrape down sides of the bowl, about 3 minutes. (Alternatively, you can use an electric stand mixer and a large bowl.)

With the mixer running on medium speed, add eggs, one at a time, letting each fully incorporate before adding the next. Add sour cream and mix until no streaks remain. (The batter may appear curdled; that’s OK.) Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed until just combined, about 20 seconds.

Scrape batter into the prepared pan and, using an offset or flexible spatula, spread it into an even layer. Sprinkle remaining 45 g (3 tablespoons) sugar over top. Using a butter knife, gently score batter down the center. Bake until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean and the top springs back lightly when touched, 75 to 90 minutes. If the cake begins to get too dark before it’s done baking, lightly tent the top with foil and continue baking.
Let cake cool in pan for 20 minutes, then carefully lift parchment to move cake to a wire rack. Let cool until just warm, about 20 minutes, while you prepare the whipped butter.

For the Whipped Butter: In the bowl of a food processor fitted with the blade attachment, pulse butter, molasses, honey, or golden syrup, and salt, pausing to scrape occasionally, until smooth and airy, about 2 minutes. Adjust with additional salt or molasses, honey, or golden syrup as needed. (The butter can also be whipped using an electric hand mixer or in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment.)
Cut the cake into thick slices and serve topped with whipped butter.

description: Dark molasses, nutty rye flour, and sour cream give this gently spiced loaf an exceptionally soft, tender crumb.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 40 min.

Optional substitutions: unsulphured light → regular molasses; light syrup → regular molasses or honey or golden syrup

Notes: A straight-sided pan, such as a Pullman loaf pan, works best for this recipe as it has a slightly larger capacity. If using a pan with tapered sides, you may want to remove about 1/2 cup of batter to ensure the pan doesn’t overflow in the oven. Use the reserved batter to make a single muffin: Place a liner in a one cup of a muffin tin, pour in batter, and bake until risen and the top springs back lightly when pressed, about 18 minutes at 350°F.

Make-ahead and storage: The leftover cake can be tightly wrapped in plastic wrap or stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
The whipped butter can be stored in an airtight container, away from direct sunlight, at room temperature for up to 2 days. It can be refrigerated for up to a week; let come to room temperature before using.
author: Zola Gregory
